chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I detest the man if I do not see him with his heel-covers on his sandals.

key_terms.مُعَقَّبَ: wearing the heel-cover / having the heel covered

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by detesting a man who does not wear his heel-covers?
ai.summary: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) expresses his dislike for a man who does not wear his heel-covers (qabab) on his sandals, indicating a concern for proper attire and neatness in footwear. This hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and maintaining a dignified appearance, reflecting the Prophet's tradition of grooming and modesty in daily conduct. It serves as a practical guideline for Muslims to ensure their clothing is secure and presentable, avoiding negligence in personal presentation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘I<sup>asws</sup> detest the man if I<sup>asws</sup> do not see a heel-covering on the sandals’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub, from al-‘ Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
I dislike a man whose footgear is without pursuer (the back part to support the back of the heels).”’
